drivers.title: OPEC+ output nears pre-war levels and IEA sees Q4 surplus; oil heads for second weekly loss
drivers.rationale: Gulf producers have restored output around Hormuz and the IEA projects a surplus -> the remaining war premium in Brent near $96 erodes -> producers lag and airlines gain. Brent is already -12.8% in 20 days and mine incidents persist, so the size is moderate.

drivers.title: Oil plunges as Trump says an Iran deal 'could happen'; Iran offers a 48-hour Hormuz reopening for sanctions relief
drivers.rationale: A deal that reopens Hormuz would remove most of the remaining war premium (Brent is still +4% in 20 days) -> producers lag, airlines gain. Monday's 11% drop already priced a lot, and the overnight US strikes show the talks can still fail, so confidence is low.

drivers.title: Tankers hit mines and a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz; ceasefire odds fall
drivers.rationale: Attacks on shipping plus falling ceasefire odds and talk of a post-midterm campaign -> energy majors gain, airlines lose. Brent is already +12% in 20 days, so the size is moderate. This cuts against yesterday's low-confidence call that diplomacy would ease the oil premium; the money has moved toward escalation.

drivers.rationale: Shuttle diplomacy is continuing, a large prisoner swap shows goodwill and a Trump-Putin-Xi meeting is next week -> somewhat higher odds of a framework deal -> Polish and reconstruction assets gain. Russia's maximalist demands (Finland out of NATO) and no breakthrough keep confidence low; EPOL is +3.1% on the week.

drivers.title: Kherson truce ends; Russian strikes resume; US approves Patriot sale to Ukraine
drivers.rationale: The end of the only working truce removes the main sign of de-escalation behind the 28-29 October calls -> lower odds of a broader deal -> Polish assets and reconstruction names lose support. EPOL fell 3% on Friday.

drivers.title: Trump sees Ukraine deal soon after Melania Trump hosts Russia-Ukraine meeting
drivers.rationale: A direct White House channel with Putin's envoy and a local ceasefire -> somewhat higher near-term deal odds -> reconstruction and Polish assets gain. The longer-dated odds fell sharply and EPOL fell 1.5%, so the money is sceptical and the call stays small.

drivers.title: Hot October CPI lifts Fed hike bets; Waller backs December hike, Goldman adds another hike
drivers.rationale: Hot core inflation plus a Fed governor committing to a hike -> markets price a sequence rather than one move (January 57%) -> yields held above 5% -> banks outperform REITs and homebuilders. December is priced at 88%, so the edge is in the follow-on hikes. Homebuilders already fell this week (NVR -9.7%).

drivers.title: Strong October jobs report revives the case for a December Fed hike; Daly says hike likely
drivers.rationale: Strong payrolls and Fed officials looking past the equity sell-off -> December hike odds rebound toward 76% -> yields supported -> banks outperform real estate and homebuilders. This reverses part of last week's dovish move, so the size is modest.

drivers.title: December Fed hike odds drop 11 points as Fed officials favour a gradual path
drivers.rationale: Tighter financial conditions after the sell-off and talk of a 'gradual' pace -> lower odds of a December hike and lower yields -> rate-sensitive real estate and homebuilders gain on banks.

picks.name: Nvidia

drivers.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns; Congress pushes China chip curbs as Bessent blames Lutnick for export-control lapses
drivers.rationale: The spy scandal, an H200 diversion to a blacklisted university and a cabinet row over lax enforcement give a Democratic Congress cover for China chip bills -> tighter enforcement and entity listings -> pressure on Nvidia and chip-tool makers with China exposure. The Xi summit next week could produce a softer White House line, so confidence is moderate.

drivers.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns; Congress pushes China chip curbs as Bessent blames Lutnick for export-control lapses
drivers.rationale: Founder-CEO exit with only an interim successor, plus rising China-sales scrutiny -> a lasting governance and political discount. The stock is already -15% in 5 days and rivals like AMD (+16%) have absorbed the rotation, so the size is small and a rebound is a real risk.

drivers.title: Trump says FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy; Democrats demand answers on AI policy
drivers.rationale: An FBI inquiry plus congressional scrutiny of Nvidia's China policy access -> lasting governance and political overhang, and risk of tougher China sales scrutiny. The money disagrees: semis bounced 5% and Polymarket odds of Nvidia being largest by market cap rose 10 points, so confidence is low.

picks.tracker_note: 2 House members bought and 3 sold (disclosed in the last 30 days)
picks.trump_note: Trump talked up on 2026-11-09: “Says Jensen Huang should stay on as Nvidia CEO, is an 'honorable guy' who had 'no idea'...”
